response: {"title":"Boundary-contract matrix before edits","intervention":"Before editing, extract from the target code and tests a compact matrix of each affected public callable's minimum, maximum, empty, malformed, and wrong-type inputs with the exact required return value or exception type and message, then make only changes whose behavior is checked against every applicable matrix row.","claim":"Compared with no appended instruction, this instruction will increase hidden boundary-and-error-semantics pass rate without exceeding the fixed deadline, while recording wall time and turns as costs.","mechanism":"The explicit per-callable matrix converts diffuse edge semantics into a finite set of auditable behavioral obligations, reducing omission errors and preventing broad fixes from silently changing exception class, message, or sentinel behavior across modules.","assumptions":["The repository code or tests expose enough evidence to infer the intended contracts.","The agent can inspect relevant files and run focused tests within the deadline.","Affected callables and boundary dimensions can be enumerated compactly."],"risks":["Contract inference may fossilize an existing bug when tests and implementation agree incorrectly.","Matrix construction consumes deadline time and may reduce implementation time.","An incomplete matrix can create false confidence and miss interaction-dependent cases.","Overly literal message matching may preserve incidental wording rather than intended semantics."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python repair tasks to the appended instruction or no appended instruction under identical deadlines, tools, and model settings; score with held-out tests emphasizing boundaries, invalid inputs, exception classes, and exact messages.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"The intervention arm has a higher held-out pass_rate, including the edge-semantics subset, with median wall_time within the fixed deadline and no material increase in turns."},"single_shot_ordinal":1}
